title: Kind Hearts, Kind Words
objectives: Use a glossary or dictionary to check what a word means
Say a sentence that uses a new vocabulary word correctly
Answer literal and inferential questions about a story
Find an event in a story that reminds me of my own experience
Use pronouns: he, him, she, her
Join two sentences with and; put quotation marks around what a character says

vocabulary.example: He shares his toys. He is a kind boy.
She helps her friend. She is a helpful girl.
He likes to laugh. He is a happy boy.
Ali was sad because he had no food.

vocabulary.definition: kind and nice to talk to
vocabulary.example: Hessa was friendly to everyone at school.

vocabulary.definition: to make a happy face with your mouth
vocabulary.example: I smile when I see my friends.

vocabulary.definition: to make a happy sound when something is funny

vocabulary.example: They like to talk all day long.

vocabulary.definition: to let someone use or have some of your things
vocabulary.example: Hessa shares her lunch with Ali.

vocabulary.definition: to make things easier for someone
what you say when you make a mistake or feel bad
vocabulary.example: He made a mistake. He is sorry.

vocabulary.definition: something that is wrong, done by accident
vocabulary.example: It is OK to make a mistake.

vocabulary.definition: a person you like and play with
vocabulary.example: My friend sits next to me.

vocabulary.definition: a present you give to someone
vocabulary.example: The teacher gave Hessa a small gift.

vocabulary.definition: a place outside where children play
what you say when someone is kind to you
vocabulary.example: Ali said, "Thank you. You are kind."

sentences.text: I smile when I see my friends.
She helps her friend. She is a helpful girl.
He shares his toys. He is a kind boy.
He made a mistake. He is sorry.
"Thank you. You are kind," said Ali.

grammar.title: he, him, she, her
explain: Pronouns are short words we use instead of a name.
he / him for a boy. she / her for a girl.
He and she DO the action. Him and her get the action: Hessa helps him.
examples: Ali is sad. Hessa helps him.
Hessa is kind. She gives him food.
The teacher sees Hessa. She gives her a gift.
He smiles because he is happy.

practice.prompt: Hessa is kind and ___ helps Ali.
Omar is my friend. I play with ___.
We say: Him is a kind boy.

grammar.title: Joining with and
explain: We can join two short sentences with and.
Hessa is kind. She helps Ali. → Hessa is kind and she helps Ali.
Remember: only one full stop, at the end.
examples: Ali is sad and Hessa helps him.
Hessa gives him food and Ali smiles.
I smile and I wave to my friends.

practice.prompt: Ali is sad. Hessa helps him. Join them:
choices: Ali is sad and Hessa helps him.
Ali is sad. and Hessa helps him.
Ali and is sad Hessa helps him.
practice.answer: Ali is sad and Hessa helps him.

practice.prompt: Hessa gives him food ___ Ali smiles.
How many full stops in a joined sentence?

practice.answer: The teacher sees Hessa and she gives her a gift.
He made a mistake and he said sorry.

grammar.title: Kind words & speech marks
explain: Kind words: Are you okay? I can help you. Thank you. You are welcome. Sorry.
Put speech marks “ ” around the exact words someone says.

practice.prompt: Your friend falls over. What do you say?
You bump into someone by mistake. You say…
A friend gives you an apple. You say…
Which sentence uses speech marks correctly?
"Thank you," said Ali. Who is talking?

reading.title: The New Girl
paragraphs: Layla was new at school. At break time, she sat alone in the playground. She was sad because she had no friends.
Omar saw Layla. He smiled and said, "Hello! Do you want to play with us?" Layla smiled too. "Yes, please!" she said.
They played a ball game. Omar kicked the ball too hard and it hit Layla's bag. Her pencils fell on the ground. "I'm sorry! It was a mistake," said Omar. He helped her pick up the pencils.
"Thank you. You are very kind," said Layla. "You are welcome," said Omar. Now Layla and Omar are good friends, and they laugh and talk every day.
